Hello World — Who I Am, What I Build, and What’s Coming Welcome to my corner of the internet. If you’ve landed here, you’re probably curious about who’s behind this blog — so let’s get into it.
About Me Hey, I’m Hanan Mohamed — a second-year Computer Science student at the University of Colombo School of Computing (UCSC). I spend most of my time writing code, breaking things on purpose, and occasionally fixing them.
My background is rooted in systems programming — C and C++ are where I feel most at home — but I enjoy the full stack of problem-solving: from low-level logic to web interfaces. I’m particularly drawn to projects that have a real structure to them: things you can architect, reason about, and build incrementally.
Outside of code, I’m genuinely interested in how the software engineering field is evolving — especially with AI reshaping the job market — and I care a lot about building skills that actually matter long-term.
This blog is where I’ll document my builds, share what I’m learning, and think out loud about the craft.
Skills & Tech Stack Here’s what I work with regularly:
Languages: C, C++, PHP, Python, JavaScript, SQL Web: HTML, CSS, Sass, MySQL, mysqli CS Fundamentals: Data Structures & Algorithms, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, Database Management, Numerical Methods Tools & Environments: Linux/Unix, Git, VS Code Currently exploring: Network tools, web security concepts, full-stack development Featured Projects 🏰 Maze of UCSC A 3D maze runner game built entirely in C, set across three floors of a block-based environment. The game features walls, stairs, poles, and special Bawana effect cells that mess with the player.
What made this project meaningful wasn’t just the game mechanics — it was the architecture. I structured it as modular files (main.c, game.c, game.h) and implemented the geometry and traversal logic from scratch. It’s the kind of project that teaches you what systems programming really feels like under pressure.
This one’s close to my heart — it lives on a university server and still surprises me sometimes.
Recent Builds Beyond featured work, here are a couple of things I’ve shipped recently:
Mail Client — A functional email client project exploring network protocols and client-server communication. Pod Scanner — A network utility tool for scanning pods/services, giving me hands-on experience with lower-level networking concepts. Both projects pushed me to get comfortable with areas I hadn’t deeply explored before — and that’s exactly the point.
What’s Coming Right now I’m building TriHackMe — a website project I’m using to sharpen my full-stack development skills. It’s a deliberate practice ground: something structured enough to be real, but flexible enough to experiment with new patterns and techniques.
I’ll be documenting the build process here as it progresses, so stay tuned if that kind of thing interests you.
Let’s Connect If you want to follow along, collaborate, or just say hi — here’s where to find me:
🐙 GitHub: github.com/hananmd 💼 LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/hanan-mohamed-b460782b2 📬 Email: hananmdofficials@gmail.com Thanks for reading the first one. More coming soon. 🚀
